trial_court: Family Court, Allahabad, Matrimonial Petition No. 172 of 1997
case_name: Monika Ohri And Ors. vs Amit Misra And Anr.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Monika Ohri and others (daughter, mother, father)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife filed for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act. Petitioner seeks to quash proceedings and restrain trial court from proceeding with petition.

legal_principles.principle: A writ of prohibition is an order directed to an inferior Tribunal forbidding it from continuing with proceeding therein on the ground that the proceeding is without or in excess of jurisdiction or contrary to the laws of the land, statutory or otherwise.
legal_principles.held: Following Mackonochie v. Lord Penzance (1881) 6 Appeal Cases 424, it was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court
cited_cases: Mackonochie v. Lord Penzance (1881) 6 Appeal Cases 424

legal_principles.principle: The jurisdiction for grant of a writ of prohibition is primarily supervisory and the object of that writ is to restrain Courts or inferior Tribunals from exercising a jurisdiction which they do not possess at all or else to prevent them for exceeding the limits of their jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: It was held by the Apex Court
cited_cases: S. Govinda Menon v. Union of India, AIR 1967 SC 1274

legal_principles.principle: The inherent power has its roots in necessity and its breadth is coextensive with the necessity.
legal_principles.held: It was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court
cited_cases: Nawabganj Sugar Mills Company Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1976 SC 1162

outcome.final_order: Proceedings of Matrimonial Petition No. 172 of 1997 are quashed, and respondent is restrained from proceeding with the petition.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
obtaining writ of Certiorari or Prohibition
